subject: Optional released lane-owner image composition and disposable owner protocol
source_of_truth: lanectl StreamStore owns lane events; immutable manifest owns catalog selection; production authority remains unchanged JSONL
backends: SQLite WAL on disposable container tmpfs
initial_state: Actual digest-identified Python3.13 image with six hash-verified owner/shared wheels
No owner database before explicit migration
Three baseline domains use registration-only fixtures with no database access

operations.name: lane.stream.append-v1
operations.synchronization: two threads meet at barrier before separate SQLite connections append expected revision zero

consistency.object: atomic scoped stream append, expected revision and principal-bound replay

assumptions.isolation: Synthetic typed invocation contexts stand in for verified identities; baseline three-owner registration never opens databases. No authentication or full HTTP startup claim.
assumptions.clock: No lease or wall-clock timing claim; thread barrier bounds the two-writer race.
assumptions.fairness: Both worker threads reach the barrier within5s; one SQLite transaction completes before the other validates expected revision.

invariants: Exactly two lane operations are added and every baseline definition is preserved
Runtime never creates an unmigrated owner database
Changed payload, stale revision and scope failures do not append events
Only one concurrent expected-revision-zero append wins
Only pinned checksum-verified wheels reach installer
faults: changed idempotent payload and different principal
oracles: actual registry input/result validation and registered owner handlers
exact baseline definition equality plus two scoped lane operations
expected refusal codes and unchanged stream contents
SQLite online backup restored through the actual owner constructor
